lecture.New_Day5Part1audio01.mp3: Welcome to Section 1: Why Aggregation Matters — From Rows to KPIs. Database tables store individual transactions, but business stakeholders need summary metrics. Aggregate functions take N input rows and collapse them into one single output metric.
lecture.New_Day5Part1audio02.mp3: Looking at the Big 5 Aggregate Functions table: First, COUNT star gives the total row count, counting all rows including NULLs. Second, COUNT of column counts only populated rows, strictly ignoring NULLs. Third, SUM of column calculates the total sum, ignoring NULLs. Fourth, AVG of column computes the arithmetic mean, ignoring NULLs in the divisor. And fifth, MIN and MAX return the smallest and largest values, also ignoring NULLs.
lecture.New_Day5Part1audio03.mp3: Here is our Core Rule of Thumb: Every aggregate function ignores NULL values — except COUNT star, which always counts the physical rows.
lecture.New_Day5Part1audio04.mp3: Section 2: COUNT — Counting Rows versus Counting Values. Always choose your COUNT variant based on what you are measuring: First, COUNT star measures Volume: How many total records exist? Second, COUNT of column measures Completeness: How many rows have a populated value? And third, COUNT DISTINCT measures Unique Entities: How many unique customers or departments exist?
lecture.New_Day5Part1audio05.mp3: Let's see COUNT Variations in Practice. Query 1 finds total headcount: SELECT COUNT star AS total employees FROM employees, returning all 15 rows. Query 2 counts staff with commissions: SELECT COUNT of commission AS commission earners FROM employees, skipping NULLs to return 6. And Query 3 counts unique departments: SELECT COUNT DISTINCT department ID AS active departments FROM employees.
lecture.New_Day5Part1audio06.mp3: Here is our Data Quality Audit Formula: Find missing or NULL values instantly with the formula: COUNT star minus COUNT of column equals Missing Rows.
lecture.New_Day5Part1audio07.mp3: Section 3: SUM and AVG — The Dangerous NULL Denominator Trap. AVG of column calculates SUM of column divided by COUNT of column. It does not divide by COUNT star. If 4 out of 15 employees have NULL commissions, AVG of commission divides by 11, not 15.
lecture.New_Day5Part1audio08.mp3: Looking at Comparing Averages With and Without NULLs: In Query 1, we get full summary stats: SUM, AVG, MIN, and MAX of salary. In Query 2, AVG of commission gives the average among commission earners only, with a divisor of 6. In Query 3, AVG of COALESCE commission 0 includes all employees, treating NULLs as zero with a divisor of 15.
lecture.New_Day5Part1audio09.mp3: Here is an essential Interview Gotcha: When asked for the average bonus across the entire company, always use AVG of COALESCE bonus 0 so employees with zero bonus are included in the denominator.
lecture.New_Day5Part1audio10.mp3: Section 4: The COALESCE Safety Net — Inside versus Outside. Placing COALESCE inside versus outside an aggregate solves two completely different business problems.
lecture.New_Day5Part1audio11.mp3: Looking at the code: Pattern A places COALESCE inside: SELECT AVG of COALESCE commission 0 to convert NULLs to zero before calculating the mean. Pattern B places COALESCE outside: SELECT COALESCE of AVG salary 0 to prevent a blank NULL when department 99 matches zero rows.
lecture.New_Day5Part1audio12.mp3: To summarize: Inside, AVG of COALESCE x 0 adjusts the average by counting zeroes. Outside, COALESCE of SUM x 0 ensures dashboard KPI cards display zero instead of a blank NULL on empty results.
lecture.New_Day5Part1audio13.mp3: Section 5: MIN and MAX — Beyond Numbers. MIN and MAX find boundary values across all SQL data types using natural ordering: For numbers, smallest and largest amounts. For dates, MIN is the earliest date and MAX is the most recent. And for strings, alphabetical first and last.
lecture.New_Day5Part1audio14.mp3: Looking at the examples: In Query 1, we find price boundaries with MIN and MAX of unit price. In Query 2, we find employee tenure range with MIN and MAX of hire date. In Query 3, we find alphabetical boundaries from first name A to last name Z.
lecture.New_Day5Part1audio15.mp3: Here is a key ISO 8601 standard note: Because dates are stored in standard YYYY-MM-DD format, alphabetical sorting matches chronological order perfectly.
lecture.New_Day5Part1audio16.mp3: Section 6: Stacking Aggregates and Expressions in One SELECT. Stack multiple aggregates in a single SELECT statement to generate a complete executive dashboard in a single table scan.
lecture.New_Day5Part1audio17.mp3: In this Executive Overview Dashboard, we select COUNT star for total headcount, SUM of salary for total payroll, rounded AVG salary, MIN hire date for company founding date, and SUM of stock quantity times unit price for total inventory value.
lecture.New_Day5Part1audio18.mp3: Notice row-level expression evaluation: In SUM of stock quantity times unit price, SQL multiplies the quantity and price for each row first, then sums the calculated results.
lecture.New_Day5Part1audio19.mp3: Section 7: NULL Deep Dive — Aggregation Edge Cases Cheat Sheet. Master these six edge cases to ace technical interviews and prevent reporting bugs.
lecture.New_Day5Part1audio20.mp3: In the Aggregation and NULL Truth Matrix: Row 1, 15 rows with 4 NULLs: COUNT star returns 15. Row 2: COUNT of commission returns 11. Row 3: AVG of commission divides only by populated entries. Row 4, a column of all NULLs: SUM and AVG return NULL. Row 5, zero rows matched: COUNT star returns 0. Row 6, zero rows matched: SUM and AVG return NULL.
lecture.New_Day5Part1audio21.mp3: Looking at the Live Demonstration Query: We compute COUNT star, COUNT of commission, AVG commission, AVG with COALESCE, and safe total payout in one single query from employees.
lecture.New_Day5Part1audio22.mp3: Here is a Pro-Tip: Always run COUNT star minus COUNT of column during initial exploratory data analysis to measure dataset cleanliness.
lecture.New_Day5Part1audio23.mp3: Caution with SUM DISTINCT: While COUNT DISTINCT is essential for unique users, SUM DISTINCT will discard legitimate identical salaries, corrupting financial totals.

questions.New_Day5Question01.mp3: Time to build a payroll summary! From employees, write a query to calculate total payroll spend as total payroll, average salary as average salary, lowest salary as min salary, and highest salary as max salary.
questions.New_Day5Question01sol.mp3: Let's write this query. SELECT SUM of salary AS total_payroll, AVG of salary AS avg_salary, MIN of salary AS min_salary, MAX of salary AS max_salary FROM employees;
questions.New_Day5Question02.mp3: How many employees are currently active? Determine how many employees have is active equal to 1, aliased as active employees.
questions.New_Day5Question02sol.mp3: Let's code this. SELECT COUNT star AS active_employees FROM employees WHERE is_active = 1;
questions.New_Day5Question03.mp3: Find the catalog price extremes! From products, return the lowest unit price as cheapest and the highest unit price as most expensive.
questions.New_Day5Question03sol.mp3: Let's write the query. SELECT MIN of unit_price AS cheapest, MAX of unit_price AS most_expensive FROM products;
questions.New_Day5Question04.mp3: Perform a commission data quality audit! In a single query from employees, return total, has commission, and no commission using COUNT star and COUNT of commission.
questions.New_Day5Question04sol.mp3: Let me write this out. SELECT COUNT star AS total, COUNT of commission AS has_commission, COUNT star minus COUNT of commission AS no_commission FROM employees;
questions.New_Day5Question05.mp3: Calculate realized shipped revenue! Find the total amount from orders where status is Shipped, aliased as shipped revenue.
questions.New_Day5Question05sol.mp3: Let's type the query. SELECT SUM of total_amount AS shipped_revenue FROM orders WHERE status = 'Shipped';
questions.New_Day5Question06.mp3: Count active department representation! Count the number of distinct department ID values in employees, aliased as num departments.
questions.New_Day5Question06sol.mp3: Let's write this. SELECT COUNT DISTINCT department_id AS num_departments FROM employees;
questions.New_Day5Question07.mp3: Calculate total warehouse inventory valuation! Compute SUM of stock quantity times unit price across all products, aliased as inventory value.
questions.New_Day5Question07sol.mp3: Let's code the inventory calculation. SELECT SUM of stock_qty times unit_price AS inventory_value FROM products;
questions.New_Day5Question08.mp3: Compute commission averages: avg non null among commission earners, and avg all across all staff treating NULL as 0.
questions.New_Day5Question08sol.mp3: Let's write the query. SELECT AVG of commission AS avg_non_null, AVG of COALESCE commission 0 AS avg_all FROM employees;
questions.New_Day5Question09.mp3: Count the luxury tier products! Count how many items in products have unit price greater than 5000, aliased as premium count.
questions.New_Day5Question09sol.mp3: Let's type this query. SELECT COUNT star AS premium_count FROM products WHERE unit_price > 5000;
questions.New_Day5Question10.mp3: Write a fault-tolerant query for department 99 using COALESCE so it returns 0 instead of NULL when no rows match.
questions.New_Day5Question10sol.mp3: Let's write the query. SELECT COALESCE of AVG salary 0 AS avg_salary FROM employees WHERE department_id = 99;
questions.New_Day5Question11.mp3: Find the peak transaction value! Return the single largest total amount from orders, aliased as largest order.
questions.New_Day5Question11sol.mp3: Let's code this. SELECT MAX of total_amount AS largest_order FROM orders;
questions.New_Day5Question12.mp3: Determine customer geographic reach! Count the number of unique regions represented in customers, aliased as num regions.
questions.New_Day5Question12sol.mp3: Let's write this out. SELECT COUNT DISTINCT region AS num_regions FROM customers;
questions.New_Day5Question13.mp3: Write a single-pass revenue segmentation returning shipped rev and processing rev using SUM with CASE WHEN.
questions.New_Day5Question13sol.mp3: Let's write the conditional aggregation. SELECT SUM of CASE WHEN status is Shipped THEN total_amount ELSE 0 END AS shipped_rev, SUM of CASE WHEN status is Processing THEN total_amount ELSE 0 END AS processing_rev FROM orders;
questions.New_Day5Question14.mp3: Calculate volume-weighted average price as SUM of unit price times quantity divided by SUM of quantity, rounded to 2 decimals.
questions.New_Day5Question14sol.mp3: Let's code the formula. SELECT ROUND of SUM of unit_price times qty times 1.0 divided by SUM of qty 2 AS weighted_avg_price FROM order_items;
questions.New_Day5Question15.mp3: Concatenate all employee first names into a comma-separated list using GROUP CONCAT, aliased as all names.
questions.New_Day5Question15sol.mp3: Let's write the query. SELECT GROUP_CONCAT of first_name with comma space AS all_names FROM employees;
